cards.text: It's feast time in Jerusalem, and the temple courts are full of people. About halfway through the feast, Jesus, God's Son, walks right up into the temple courts and starts teaching. No back door. No whisper. Right out in the OPEN.

cards.question: The Jews in the temple courts are amazed at Jesus' teaching. What do they want to know?

answers.text: How He got such learning without studying
Why He waited so long to come and teach
Who gave Him permission to teach right here

cards.question: Jesus answers the Jews' question about His learning. Where does He say His teaching comes from?

answers.text: From the One who sent Him
From years of reading the Scriptures

cards.text: So Jesus is NOT freestyling up there. His teaching comes from the One who sent Him, and He says there's a way a person can know that for sure.

cards.question: Jesus says only people who studied under great teachers can know whether His teaching is from God.
Jesus says someone who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory. But the one who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of ___.

cards.text: Jesus brings up Moses, Israel's leader long ago, who gave them the law. Then He says, "Yet not one of you keeps it."

cards.question: Jesus has just told the crowd that not one of them keeps the law of Moses. What does He ask them next?

answers.text: Why are you trying to kill Me
Why do you doubt My teaching
Why did you come to this feast

cards.question: When Jesus asks why they're trying to kill Him, the crowd admits that someone is.

cards.text: The crowd fires back, "You have a demon," and then asks, "Who is trying to kill You?" ONE question went in, and an accusation PLUS a question came out. That's a two-for-one nobody ordered.
Jesus answers, "I did one miracle, and you are all amazed." Then He points out that because Moses gave them circumcision, they circumcise a boy on the Sabbath.

cards.question: Jesus adds a side note: circumcision didn't start with Moses but with the patriarchs.

cards.text: Now Jesus brings it home. If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so the law of Moses won't be broken, why are they angry with Him?

cards.question: Jesus asks why the crowd is angry with Him over something He did on the Sabbath. What was it?
Jesus finishes by telling the crowd to stop judging by outward ___ and start judging ___.

cards.text: Then some people of Jerusalem start asking, "Isn't this the man they are trying to kill?" Somebody in this city did NOT get the same memo as that crowd.

cards.question: As Jesus speaks out in the open, the rulers aren't saying anything to Him.

cards.text: So the people wonder, "Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?" And then, I kid you not, they talk themselves right back out of it.

cards.question: Why do the people of Jerusalem doubt that Jesus is the Christ?

answers.text: They know where He is from

cards.text: Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cries out, "You know Me, and you know where I am from." Then He says He hasn't come on His own, and the One who sent Him is true.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd in the temple courts that they know the One who sent Him.

cards.text: But Jesus knows the One who sent Him, because He is from Him. Right then, they try to seize Jesus, and the hands start reaching.

cards.question: They try to seize Jesus in the temple courts, but no one lays a hand on Him. Why not?

answers.text: His hour had not yet come
His disciples stood in the way

cards.question: Many in the crowd believe in Jesus. They ask whether the Christ will perform more ___ than this man.

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of religious leaders, hear the crowd whispering these things about Jesus. I bet it's like the whole office going silent when the boss walks by.

cards.question: Once the Pharisees hear the crowd whispering about Jesus, they team up with the chief priests. What do they do?

answers.text: Ask Jesus to teach them more
Order the crowd to go home

cards.text: So Jesus says He'll be with them only a little while longer. Then He's leaving, and He is NOT dropping off a forwarding address.

cards.question: After a little while, Jesus says, He is going to the One who ___ Him.
Jesus tells the people in the temple courts that they will look for Him and find Him.
The Jews ask one another where Jesus could go that they won't find Him. What do they guess?

answers.text: To the Jews scattered among the Greeks
Back up north to the towns of Galilee
Out into the wilderness near the Jordan

cards.text: They keep asking each other what He means about looking and not finding, and about a place they cannot come. Stick around, friend, because Jesus isn't done at this feast.

findings.problem: The opening card has five sentences: 'It's feast time...', 'About halfway through...', 'No back door.', 'No whisper.', 'Right out in the OPEN.' The passage also starts mid-story, but the card never gives the context that some want to kill Jesus. Card 8 depends on that context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The first half of the card repeats the answer card 3 just revealed: 'His teaching comes from the One who sent Him.' That is a recap, not new movement.

John 7:17 gives the way a person can know Jesus' teaching is from God: if anyone desires to do His will. No card ever tells this. Card 4 says 'there's a way,' and card 5 only rules out studying under great teachers, so the baker never learns the actual condition.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: No earlier card says anyone wants Jesus dead, so 'Why are you trying to kill Me' can only be picked by luck. 'Why do you doubt My teaching' looks like the reasoned pick. The setup needs context, for example on the opening card.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the crowd's reply, 'ONE question went in...', and 'That's a two-for-one nobody ordered.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No story card sets up John 7:24. The card just blanks out the words of Jesus' line ('outward ___ ... judging ___'), so it tests recall of wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The statement presents 'the rulers aren't saying anything to Him' as narration. In John 7:26 it is what some of the people of Jerusalem say. The card should frame it as their words.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The priests have rejected Him' can be argued as true in this passage. In John 7:32 the chief priests send officers to arrest Jesus.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'Right then' adds a timing that John 7:30 doesn't give. The text only says 'So they tried to seize Him.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. In John 7:32 the Pharisees overhear the crowd whispering. An office going silent when the boss walks by is whispering stopping, the opposite. A stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke says Jesus is 'NOT dropping off a forwarding address.' In John 7:33 He does say where He is going: to the One who sent Him. The joke muddies a fact the text states.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The 'no forwarding address' line tells the baker that Jesus can't be found. That gives away card 14, which asks whether they will look for Him and find Him.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
